Many critics still realised that it was one of the best and most original films of 2010. With its cult success repeated in the US, Wheatley has quickly followed it with the most assured and troubling British horror film in many years. Kill List confirms his promise while pinning you to your seat with scenes of cold nightmare. We begin in a deceptively similar milieu to Down Terrace , at the suburban home of working-class Jay (Neil Maskell) and wife Shel (MyAnna Buring). When Jay follows a blazing row by telling their adored seven-year-old son a bedtime story about Daddy’s recent time in Iraq we’re assured that, for all his mood swings, he’s a loving family man. The arrival of fellow veteran Gal (Michael Smiley) and apparently dim new girlfriend Fiona (Emma Fryer) for the sort of boozy, chaotic dinner party also familiar from Down Terrace deepens the belief that we’re on familiar ground. When Gal offers Jay the financial lifeline of a spot of freelance assassination, we sit back to enjoy Wheatley (co-writer as well as director) adding cleverly bantering working-class hitmen to his debut’s gangsters. Both Wheatley’s films are comedy-dramas, in the way that most lives are. Jay’s verbal demolition of a bunch of happy-clappy Christians getting on his nerves during hotel breakfast is especially funny. But no more so than the scene when Gal, told by Jay to wait five minutes before following him into a warehouse, creeps through it to the sound of ominous thuds, and finally stumbles upon his pal drenched in blood, beating his hapless quarry to a pulp. “Was that five minutes?” Jay, lost in his work, enquires. We’ve already been through the gruelling scene on which Kill List pivots. Jay (pictured) , provoked by laptop footage we never see of screaming people (tortured children?), takes a hammer to the man he blames, who thanks him between screams, till he has no mouth. The camera doesn’t flinch when you hope it will. It’s a sort of sequel to Reservoir Dogs ’s infamous ear-slicing (more visceral and far less funny on first viewing than it seems now). The careful opposite of Saw ’s torture porn, it resensitises you to violence and agony when you thought you’d seen it all. Martin Pavey’s subliminally sickening sound design adds to the fear of unguessable awfulness, in the second half of the film that now looms. The only clue to what follows rests in the Client (Struan Rodger), a formidably dissolute, almost silent aristocrat, whose mouth hangs open in predatory amusement at the hitmen he’s hired. The wound he carves in Jay’s palm to sign their deal in blood becomes infected, along with Jay’s grip on reality. There’s a touch of Rosemary’s Baby as even the doctor that the self-medicating, frightened and volatile veteran is sent to seems part of a paranoid plot. Kill List is set partly in the blank motorway hotels that dot modern England (though filmed around Sheffield, it’s this anonymous interzone which gives its sense of place). But by its final reel, older, rustic horrors are intruding. The giddying lurch when this happens teeters on the risible, dispelling the grim urban fear preceding it. It took just minutes for the ferocity of the subsequent nightmare to breathlessly snuff my resistance. Even a final scene which first struck me as disappointingly obvious lodged in my mind later. Kill List combines smoothly efficient construction worthy of John Carpenter with mystery it refuses to dispel; cool reality with something feverish. It feels like a landmark British film, another step in Wheatley’s resurrecting of moribund genres he approaches with respect, and makes uncomfortably real. Season 4 is heading for some major changes. Not only is Liam Hemsworth taking over the lead role following Henry Cavill 's departure, but the story has reached a new height as Geralt has left his neutrality behind ahead of an inevitable war. Overall, Season 3 leaves the heroes in a precarious place ahead of the show's return , setting up an eventful Season 4 . Ciri Is Being Hunted in 'The Witcher' Season 3 Geralt (Henry Cavill), Ciri (Freya Allan), and Yennefer (Anya Chalotra) in The Witcher Season 3 Episode 1 Image via Netflix Following their earlier division, The Witcher Season 3 throws Geralt and Yennefer ( Anya Chalotra ) together as they go on the run with Ciri ( Freya Allan ) . Though Yennefer attempts to teach the girl magic, progress is slow, especially with Rience ( Sam Woolf ) sending people after them. Their plan changes when Rience sends a monster to find Ciri. Though Geralt and Yennefer save her, this dangerous threat signals that they cannot remain hidden. Instead, they lay a trap for Rience, hoping to use Ciri as bait and Jaskier ( Joey Batey ) as a decoy protector. While Ciri and the caravan fight off his allies, Rience portals away, and Yennefer helps Geralt to follow. Geralt breaks Rience's hands and notes the landscape out the window before returning to the battle, which has only grown worse because of the Elves' arrival. Despite the fractured trust of her people, Francesca ( Mecia Simson ) believes Ciri is their new hope, and they are now pursuing the girl as well. Despite the battle, Geralt, Ciri, Yennefer, and Jaskier make it safely away, and Geralt has gained an idea of where to look for Rience while his strange portal leads Yennefer to suspect the existence of another rogue mage . Geralt gathers the information he can before going after Rience. When he reaches the place from the portal, he expects a trap, but he hears the whispers of young girls, only to discover a monster made out of their remains and one girl still alive. Geralt slays the creature, saving the last girl, who recognizes Geralt and calls herself Ciri. Fake Ciri is only occasionally lucid, but together, Geralt and Jaskier learn that her name is Teryn ( Frances Pooley ) and she remembers a woman with a funny voice and a man with a scar, whom she met at Aretuza, but she doesn't give a name. 'The Witcher' Season 3 Puts Yennefer in a Difficult Position Yennefer (Anya Chalotra) and Tessaia (Myanna Buring) in The Witcher Season 3 Episode 4 Image via Netflix Yennefer reaches out to her mentor and former teacher, Tissaia ( MyAnna Buring ), in hopes of getting help to train Ciri. As they travel, Ciri's visions are getting more frequent, and she tries to act on them despite Yennefer's warnings about consequences. Yennefer is unsure of the welcome that awaits her at Aretuza, and before making herself known to the Brotherhood, she meets with Tissaia , learning that her welcome will be what she fears. Meanwhile, Ciri exposes a con artist for passing off a wyvern as a basilisk and then has to slay the mistreated creature when it gets out. Yet, when Ciri is reunited with Yennefer, she meets several mages, who do not give her a favorable impression of Aretuza. The situation puts both Ciri and Yennefer on edge, and they argue until Ciri runs away to look for Geralt. The Wild Hunt chases her, but Geralt finds her and sends them away. After Ciri visited their world in Season 2 , the Wild Hunt is free, which is why Ciri must learn to control her abilities. Every Character Is Plotting Something in 'The Witcher' Season 3 Dijkstra (Graham Mctavish) and Philippa (Cassie Clare) in The Witcher Season 3 Image via Netflix The Witcher has many moving stories , such as the Redanian storyline. The sorceress Philippa ( Cassie Clare ) and spymaster Dijkstra ( Graham McTavish ) are working to deliver Ciri into the hands of King Vizimir ( Ed Birch ). Though Philippa tries to get Jaskier's help, the bard only offers to talk to Geralt. When Vizimir assigns his brother, Prince Radovid ( Hugh Skinner ), to help, Philippa believes the prince could be useful, especially considering Jaskier develops feelings for him. Radovid reveals that Vizimir made a deal to turn Ciri over to Nilfgaard behind Dijkstra's back. Believing the issue to be Vizimir's queen, Dijkstra has her killed, framing Nilfgaard. Though Radovid is horrified, Dijkstra leaves him with no option but to go along with the plan. Fringilla ( Mimî M. Khayisa ), a sorceress working in the service of Nilfgaard, also returns, though she is being held as a taster for Emhyr ( Bart Edwards ), the White Flame. Though no one has managed to escape Emhyr's clutches, Fringilla takes a chance by climbing into a body bag, being thrown out with the other deceased. Also in Nilfgaard is Cahir ( Eamon Farren ), who takes his Elf friend, Gallatin ( Robbie Amell ), to Emhyr. Though Gallatin hopes to take control from Francesca, Emhyr has no desire to divide the Elves. Instead, he has Cahir prove his loyalty by killing Gallatin. With renewed faith in him, Emhyr sends Cahir to meet Francesca, proposing an alliance in the search for Ciri, which she begrudgingly accepts. Aretuza Is Not Safe in 'The Witcher' Season 3 Anna Shaffer as Triss Merigold kneeling on the floor in The Witcher Image via Netflix In Aretuza, Yennefer apologizes to the Brotherhood and proposes a conclave to promote unity. Though many don't want to listen, they accept her proposal because Vilgefortz ( Mahesh Jadu ) speaks up for her, thanks to his relationship with Tissaia. Yennefer also visits Redania to ensure Philippa's attendance. Despite her success, on the way back, her portal is corrupted , proving that Aretuza isn't safe. That idea is reinforced as Triss ( Anna Shaffer ) looks into the missing novices. She encounters Istredd ( Royce Pierreson ), who is still searching for the Book of Monoliths, and they piece their problems together. The missing girls are half-Elven, and someone in Aretuza has the book that could banish them. Tipped off by her suspicions about Yennefer's attack, Triss learns that the Book of Monoliths is in a safe in Stregobor's (Lars Mikkelsen) office , which points to his duplicity. Posts 2 By Adam Blevins Oct 7, 2025 'The Witcher' Season 3 Lets Ciri and Geralt Work Together Ciri (Freya Allan) with a sword raised and Jaskier (Joey Batey) and Geralt (Henry Cavill) behind her in The Witcher Season 3 Image via Netflix Geralt, Ciri, and Jaskier return to Aretuza, getting trapped on a boat with Jaskier's musical rival while a monster chases them. This gives Ciri a chance to show off her monster-fighting abilities alongside Geralt . Though her success leads Ciri to consider a different life, Geralt has to explain to her what he saw, telling her she cannot hide forever. They arrive in Aretuza before the event begins, allowing Yennefer and Ciri to make up before the girl is forced to hide in a nearby cabin with Jaskier to watch her. During the night, Jaskier encounters Radovid , and they kiss. 'The Witcher' Season 3 Brings Chaos to the Mages' Ball Yennefer (Anya Chalotra) and Geralt (Henry Cavill) in The Witcher Season 3 Image via Netflix Geralt attends the Brotherhood's ball with Yennefer, ready to attack Stregobor, but Yennefer wants a more subtle approach. Geralt and Yennefer are separated throughout the night, with each talking to different groups. Philippa urges Yennefer to leave the Brotherhood while Geralt speaks to Vilgefortz, who unsuccessfully suggests that Geralt join his cause. Meanwhile, Istredd asks Yennefer for help stealing the Book of Monoliths from Stregobor. Geralt and Istredd stage a distraction while Yennefer sneaks off to find the evidence . Stregobor denies his involvement, but is imprisoned. However, as Yennefer and Geralt talk about the night, they realize they were wrong. First, they identify Lydia ( Aisha Fabienne Ross ), a mage who can only speak telepathically, as the woman Teryn described. Then, they connect her earrings and Tissaia's amulet from Vilgefortz to the place Geralt found. Too late, they realize Vilgefortz is the rogue mage , and Aretuza is now under attack. Geralt is taken prisoner, but Yennefer escapes, going after Ciri. War Breaks Out in 'The Witcher' Season 3 Dijkstra and his allies hope to purge the Brotherhood of evil, accusing Vilgefortz of working with Nilfgaard. While the argument ensues, Geralt notices another attack coming, and he breaks free to find Ciri. Tissaia sides with Vilgefortz until he reveals the truth by letting the Elven warriors known as the Scoia'tael in to burn Aretuza down , adding a new enemy to the battle. After spending the night with Radovid, Jaskier loses Ciri, though he does realize that was what Radovid planned. Ciri has escaped, and, though killing Lydia briefly delays her, Yennefer ultimately finds Ciri. Rience reaches them as well, but Geralt arrives and beheads him. However, the family must separate as Yennefer returns to protect Aretuza while Geralt and Ciri try to escape. Yennefer joins the all-out battle between the Brotherhood and the Elves. In the chaos, Stregobor sacrifices himself, Vilgefortz recovers the Book of Monoliths, and Yennefer gets Tissaia out at the last minute. As they leave, Geralt and Ciri encounter Cahir, whom Ciri blames for destroying her home. However, Cahir, who has rethought his loyalties, surrenders to Ciri. But when the Elves find them, he temporarily rescinds the offer to protect her. Yet, the Elves are not Geralt and Ciri's only enemy. Vilgefortz finds them, and Geralt sends Ciri on alone. In the fight, Geralt is badly injured , and when Vilgefortz wins, he follows Ciri into the tunnels just before the tower explodes. In the end, the Elves leave without Ciri, the mages watch the destruction of Aretuza, and Triss finds an injured Geralt. Jaskier also discovers a distraught Radovid in the aftermath and gives him a way home despite their differences. Though everyone suspects Ciri is dead, she falls into the desert of Korath and must survive on her own. Throughout her journey, Ciri experiences various hallucinations, including long-dead family members, a unicorn, and a mysterious woman called Falka ( Hiftu Quasem ), a legendary figure who is considered a monster. Ciri's unicorn friend is attacked, and to heal it, she lets Falka tempt her into fire magic , scaring the unicorn. Though Falka tells her to give in to it, Ciri releases the magic quickly. The next thing Ciri remembers is waking up to strangers, who take her captive. 'The Witcher' Season 3's Finale Sets Up Big Threats for Every Character Henry Cavill as Geralt of Rivia fighting several knights in The Witcher Image via Netflix After the events at Aretuza, Tissaia dies by suicide over her immense guilt and Vilgefortz's betrayal. In the aftermath, Yennefer, Triss, and the other mages make it their mission to rebuild the Brotherhood and eliminate Vilgefortz. Meanwhile, Geralt heals from his wounds in Brokilon, where Jaskier brings the news that Nilfgaard has seemingly found Ciri. Yennefer visits him, with each blaming themselves for what happened to Ciri. She heals Geralt, and he promises to find Ciri while Yennefer builds a safe place for them to return to. In Redania, Vizimir accuses Dijkstra of failure, wanting Philippa killed as punishment. However, Philippa has Vizimir assassinated, making an unwilling Radovid the new king. Redania isn't the only country facing changes . Fringilla and Francesca, who reunited during the battle, propose a deal with Emhyr to make Fringilla the governor of Cintra, where the Elves can live. Emhyr gives them harsh terms, and still, Francesca is ready to agree until Fringilla reveals that Emhyr killed Francesca's baby , leading the mourning mother to swear revenge. Emhyr has a major win when Ciri seems to return home; however, the girl presented to him is Teryn , and Emhyr doesn't seem to realize it. The real Ciri is held captive until she teams up with another prisoner. The other prisoners' friends, a criminal group known as the Rats , come to save him, including Mistle ( Christelle Elwin ), whom Ciri briefly met before. In the fight, Ciri kills her captor, showing a more brutal side of herself and impressing the Rats. Now healed, Geralt leaves Brokilon to rescue who he thinks is Ciri from Emhyr's clutches . He and Jaskier pass a corrupt set of Nilfgaardian soldiers, and though Geralt manages to bribe them, the girl behind them cannot. Geralt takes action , forsaking his neutrality and killing the guards. His new ally, Milva ( Meng'er Zhang ), a skilled archer from Brokilon, also commits herself to Geralt's new cause. Between Geralt's determination to act, Yennefer's mission to rebuild, and Ciri's new companions, The Witcher Season 3 leaves many stories open, promising an action-packed return as the Netflix series moves towards its impending end . The Witcher Season 4 premieres October 30 on Netflix. But I will say this: Kill L ist isn’t afraid to go there. This is an exceptionally violent and dark film, which is funny considering that it initially plays out like a domestic drama. Kill List introduces us to former soldier Jay (Neil Maskell) and his wife, Shel (MyAnna Buring). They live in the suburbs with their son, Sam (Harry Simpson). This might seem like the perfect situation, but the atmosphere inside the home is tense. Jay’s been unemployed for the past year, and his inability to find work is taking its toll on the family. Shel decides to throw a dinner party and invites Jay’s friend and former colleague, Gal (Michael Smiley), and his girlfriend, Fiona (Emma Fryer). Perhaps this dinner will be good for Jay—Gal has a job offer for him. Better yet, they can work together. Just like old times. As Wheatley put it, this is a “war movie,” but I also think this is a movie about masculinity in crisis, gender roles, domesticity, and how far a man is willing to go to maintain the status quo. Jay wants so badly to be the kind of man who can take control, who can provide for his family and also be there for his friends, but he quickly finds out that none of these things are possible without some kind of sacrifice. Kill List is about what it looks like to uphold the social contract—that is, what you are willing to give up in order to enjoy social benefits and protection, especially as a man. Sergei, a former Russian military intelligence officer who acted as a double agent for Britain’s MI6 in the 1990s and early 2000s, had relocated to the UK in 2010 under a spy exchange agreement and was living in Salisbury, but evidently never felt entirely safe. As he was quoted as saying in this BBC One dramatisation of the affair, “Putin’s gonna get me”. Typically of the goings-on in the worlds of espionage and realpolitik , the facts remain frustratingly elusive. Two Russian intelligence agents, Alexander Petrov and Ruslan Boshirov (possibly not their real names), were cited by the British government as the prime suspects in the attempted killings, but the Russians claimed they were innocent civilians. Almost everybody else agreed among themselves that the Russians must have been responsible, without ever quite pinning down conclusive proof. In this three-part series, writers Declan Lawn and Adam Patterson told the story largely as the British public perceived it through the media, from the discovery of the Skripals in a semi-comatose state on a Salisbury park bench, through the police investigation and the health-and-safety panic as the various authorities battled to ensure that the mysterious poison couldn’t spread and cause more mayhem. Director Saul Dibb had done a capable job of shooting the story like a high-quality thriller. The imagery was graded in moody blues and fizzing oranges, the tension discreetly cranked up by ever-circling police helicopters and camerawork that stalked its characters with quiet malevolence. However, the problem with constructing the story only from the observable facts meant that there couldn’t be a dramatically satisfying solution, since the culprits were never brought to book and the mystery just gradually fizzled out. There was no effort here to probe behind the headlines, and the Russian suspects were merely glimpsed in passing on a TV in the background. Thus, The Salisbury Poisonings relied on the performances of its central characters to hold our attention and infuse some emotional depth into the proceedings. Pick of the bunch was Anne-Marie Duff as Wiltshire’s Director of Public Health Tracy Daszkiewicz, growing increasingly haggard and hollow-eyed and getting ever rattier with her husband as the potential scale of the problem dawned on her. The invisible novichok can apparently retain its lethal potency for 50 years, and tracking down every last spot of the stuff was virtually impossible. However, Daskiewicz’s insistence on locking down the centre of Salisbury and instigating a thorough track-and-trace procedure might have been a valuable model to follow in the coronavirus crisis. Also putting in some dogged grunt work was Rafe Spall as DS Nick Bailey (pictured above) , who received a hefty dose of novichok from the handle of the Skripals’ front door and ended up in intensive care, fighting a physical and mental battle against a substance which seems to send every organ in the body, including the brain, haywire. The real-life Bailey is still in a prolonged state of recuperation. The sole fatality from the novichok attack was Dawn Sturgess, who was infected by spraying herself with what she assumed to be perfume given to her by her partner Charlie Rowley (Johnny Harris). MyAnna Buring played the troubled, alcoholic Sturgess with understated conviction, but the randomness of her fate made it difficult to integrate her and Rowley into the main story (Buring and Harris pictured above ). One of the drawbacks of the series was that it gave little sense of how much time was elapsing between events, but Sturgess and Rowley’s encounter with novichok came nearly four months after the Skripals fell ill. This was a sinister and depressing story, but not an ideal candidate for dramatisation. The missing pieces of the jigsaw meant that it was impossible to derive any meaningful message from it, other than that terrible things can happen to innocent people. Many critics still realised that it was one of the best and most original films of 2010. With its cult success repeated in the US, Wheatley has quickly followed it with the most assured and troubling British horror film in many years. Kill List confirms his promise while pinning you to your seat with scenes of cold nightmare. We begin in a deceptively similar milieu to Down Terrace , at the suburban home of working-class Jay (Neil Maskell) and wife Shel (MyAnna Buring). When Jay follows a blazing row by telling their adored seven-year-old son a bedtime story about Daddy’s recent time in Iraq we’re assured that, for all his mood swings, he’s a loving family man. The arrival of fellow veteran Gal (Michael Smiley) and apparently dim new girlfriend Fiona (Emma Fryer) for the sort of boozy, chaotic dinner party also familiar from Down Terrace deepens the belief that we’re on familiar ground. When Gal offers Jay the financial lifeline of a spot of freelance assassination, we sit back to enjoy Wheatley (co-writer as well as director) adding cleverly bantering working-class hitmen to his debut’s gangsters. Both Wheatley’s films are comedy-dramas, in the way that most lives are. Jay’s verbal demolition of a bunch of happy-clappy Christians getting on his nerves during hotel breakfast is especially funny. But no more so than the scene when Gal, told by Jay to wait five minutes before following him into a warehouse, creeps through it to the sound of ominous thuds, and finally stumbles upon his pal drenched in blood, beating his hapless quarry to a pulp. “Was that five minutes?” Jay, lost in his work, enquires. We’ve already been through the gruelling scene on which Kill List pivots. Jay (pictured) , provoked by laptop footage we never see of screaming people (tortured children?), takes a hammer to the man he blames, who thanks him between screams, till he has no mouth. The camera doesn’t flinch when you hope it will. It’s a sort of sequel to Reservoir Dogs ’s infamous ear-slicing (more visceral and far less funny on first viewing than it seems now). The careful opposite of Saw ’s torture porn, it resensitises you to violence and agony when you thought you’d seen it all. Martin Pavey’s subliminally sickening sound design adds to the fear of unguessable awfulness, in the second half of the film that now looms. The only clue to what follows rests in the Client (Struan Rodger), a formidably dissolute, almost silent aristocrat, whose mouth hangs open in predatory amusement at the hitmen he’s hired. The wound he carves in Jay’s palm to sign their deal in blood becomes infected, along with Jay’s grip on reality. There’s a touch of Rosemary’s Baby as even the doctor that the self-medicating, frightened and volatile veteran is sent to seems part of a paranoid plot. Kill List is set partly in the blank motorway hotels that dot modern England (though filmed around Sheffield, it’s this anonymous interzone which gives its sense of place). But by its final reel, older, rustic horrors are intruding. The giddying lurch when this happens teeters on the risible, dispelling the grim urban fear preceding it. It took just minutes for the ferocity of the subsequent nightmare to breathlessly snuff my resistance. Even a final scene which first struck me as disappointingly obvious lodged in my mind later. Kill List combines smoothly efficient construction worthy of John Carpenter with mystery it refuses to dispel; cool reality with something feverish. It feels like a landmark British film, another step in Wheatley’s resurrecting of moribund genres he approaches with respect, and makes uncomfortably real. Season 4 is heading for some major changes. Not only is Liam Hemsworth taking over the lead role following Henry Cavill 's departure, but the story has reached a new height as Geralt has left his neutrality behind ahead of an inevitable war. Overall, Season 3 leaves the heroes in a precarious place ahead of the show's return , setting up an eventful Season 4 . Ciri Is Being Hunted in 'The Witcher' Season 3 Geralt (Henry Cavill), Ciri (Freya Allan), and Yennefer (Anya Chalotra) in The Witcher Season 3 Episode 1 Image via Netflix Following their earlier division, The Witcher Season 3 throws Geralt and Yennefer ( Anya Chalotra ) together as they go on the run with Ciri ( Freya Allan ) . Though Yennefer attempts to teach the girl magic, progress is slow, especially with Rience ( Sam Woolf ) sending people after them. Their plan changes when Rience sends a monster to find Ciri. Though Geralt and Yennefer save her, this dangerous threat signals that they cannot remain hidden. Instead, they lay a trap for Rience, hoping to use Ciri as bait and Jaskier ( Joey Batey ) as a decoy protector. While Ciri and the caravan fight off his allies, Rience portals away, and Yennefer helps Geralt to follow. Geralt breaks Rience's hands and notes the landscape out the window before returning to the battle, which has only grown worse because of the Elves' arrival. Despite the fractured trust of her people, Francesca ( Mecia Simson ) believes Ciri is their new hope, and they are now pursuing the girl as well. Despite the battle, Geralt, Ciri, Yennefer, and Jaskier make it safely away, and Geralt has gained an idea of where to look for Rience while his strange portal leads Yennefer to suspect the existence of another rogue mage . Geralt gathers the information he can before going after Rience. When he reaches the place from the portal, he expects a trap, but he hears the whispers of young girls, only to discover a monster made out of their remains and one girl still alive. Geralt slays the creature, saving the last girl, who recognizes Geralt and calls herself Ciri. Fake Ciri is only occasionally lucid, but together, Geralt and Jaskier learn that her name is Teryn ( Frances Pooley ) and she remembers a woman with a funny voice and a man with a scar, whom she met at Aretuza, but she doesn't give a name. 'The Witcher' Season 3 Puts Yennefer in a Difficult Position Yennefer (Anya Chalotra) and Tessaia (Myanna Buring) in The Witcher Season 3 Episode 4 Image via Netflix Yennefer reaches out to her mentor and former teacher, Tissaia ( MyAnna Buring ), in hopes of getting help to train Ciri. As they travel, Ciri's visions are getting more frequent, and she tries to act on them despite Yennefer's warnings about consequences. Yennefer is unsure of the welcome that awaits her at Aretuza, and before making herself known to the Brotherhood, she meets with Tissaia , learning that her welcome will be what she fears. Meanwhile, Ciri exposes a con artist for passing off a wyvern as a basilisk and then has to slay the mistreated creature when it gets out. Yet, when Ciri is reunited with Yennefer, she meets several mages, who do not give her a favorable impression of Aretuza. The situation puts both Ciri and Yennefer on edge, and they argue until Ciri runs away to look for Geralt. The Wild Hunt chases her, but Geralt finds her and sends them away. After Ciri visited their world in Season 2 , the Wild Hunt is free, which is why Ciri must learn to control her abilities. Every Character Is Plotting Something in 'The Witcher' Season 3 Dijkstra (Graham Mctavish) and Philippa (Cassie Clare) in The Witcher Season 3 Image via Netflix The Witcher has many moving stories , such as the Redanian storyline. The sorceress Philippa ( Cassie Clare ) and spymaster Dijkstra ( Graham McTavish ) are working to deliver Ciri into the hands of King Vizimir ( Ed Birch ). Though Philippa tries to get Jaskier's help, the bard only offers to talk to Geralt. When Vizimir assigns his brother, Prince Radovid ( Hugh Skinner ), to help, Philippa believes the prince could be useful, especially considering Jaskier develops feelings for him. Radovid reveals that Vizimir made a deal to turn Ciri over to Nilfgaard behind Dijkstra's back. Believing the issue to be Vizimir's queen, Dijkstra has her killed, framing Nilfgaard. Though Radovid is horrified, Dijkstra leaves him with no option but to go along with the plan. Fringilla ( Mimî M. Khayisa ), a sorceress working in the service of Nilfgaard, also returns, though she is being held as a taster for Emhyr ( Bart Edwards ), the White Flame. Though no one has managed to escape Emhyr's clutches, Fringilla takes a chance by climbing into a body bag, being thrown out with the other deceased. Also in Nilfgaard is Cahir ( Eamon Farren ), who takes his Elf friend, Gallatin ( Robbie Amell ), to Emhyr. Though Gallatin hopes to take control from Francesca, Emhyr has no desire to divide the Elves. Instead, he has Cahir prove his loyalty by killing Gallatin. With renewed faith in him, Emhyr sends Cahir to meet Francesca, proposing an alliance in the search for Ciri, which she begrudgingly accepts. Aretuza Is Not Safe in 'The Witcher' Season 3 Anna Shaffer as Triss Merigold kneeling on the floor in The Witcher Image via Netflix In Aretuza, Yennefer apologizes to the Brotherhood and proposes a conclave to promote unity. Though many don't want to listen, they accept her proposal because Vilgefortz ( Mahesh Jadu ) speaks up for her, thanks to his relationship with Tissaia. Yennefer also visits Redania to ensure Philippa's attendance. Despite her success, on the way back, her portal is corrupted , proving that Aretuza isn't safe. That idea is reinforced as Triss ( Anna Shaffer ) looks into the missing novices. She encounters Istredd ( Royce Pierreson ), who is still searching for the Book of Monoliths, and they piece their problems together. The missing girls are half-Elven, and someone in Aretuza has the book that could banish them. Tipped off by her suspicions about Yennefer's attack, Triss learns that the Book of Monoliths is in a safe in Stregobor's (Lars Mikkelsen) office , which points to his duplicity. Posts 2 By Adam Blevins Oct 7, 2025 'The Witcher' Season 3 Lets Ciri and Geralt Work Together Ciri (Freya Allan) with a sword raised and Jaskier (Joey Batey) and Geralt (Henry Cavill) behind her in The Witcher Season 3 Image via Netflix Geralt, Ciri, and Jaskier return to Aretuza, getting trapped on a boat with Jaskier's musical rival while a monster chases them. This gives Ciri a chance to show off her monster-fighting abilities alongside Geralt . Though her success leads Ciri to consider a different life, Geralt has to explain to her what he saw, telling her she cannot hide forever. They arrive in Aretuza before the event begins, allowing Yennefer and Ciri to make up before the girl is forced to hide in a nearby cabin with Jaskier to watch her. During the night, Jaskier encounters Radovid , and they kiss. 'The Witcher' Season 3 Brings Chaos to the Mages' Ball Yennefer (Anya Chalotra) and Geralt (Henry Cavill) in The Witcher Season 3 Image via Netflix Geralt attends the Brotherhood's ball with Yennefer, ready to attack Stregobor, but Yennefer wants a more subtle approach. Geralt and Yennefer are separated throughout the night, with each talking to different groups. Philippa urges Yennefer to leave the Brotherhood while Geralt speaks to Vilgefortz, who unsuccessfully suggests that Geralt join his cause. Meanwhile, Istredd asks Yennefer for help stealing the Book of Monoliths from Stregobor. Geralt and Istredd stage a distraction while Yennefer sneaks off to find the evidence . Stregobor denies his involvement, but is imprisoned. However, as Yennefer and Geralt talk about the night, they realize they were wrong. First, they identify Lydia ( Aisha Fabienne Ross ), a mage who can only speak telepathically, as the woman Teryn described. Then, they connect her earrings and Tissaia's amulet from Vilgefortz to the place Geralt found. Too late, they realize Vilgefortz is the rogue mage , and Aretuza is now under attack. Geralt is taken prisoner, but Yennefer escapes, going after Ciri. War Breaks Out in 'The Witcher' Season 3 Dijkstra and his allies hope to purge the Brotherhood of evil, accusing Vilgefortz of working with Nilfgaard. While the argument ensues, Geralt notices another attack coming, and he breaks free to find Ciri. Tissaia sides with Vilgefortz until he reveals the truth by letting the Elven warriors known as the Scoia'tael in to burn Aretuza down , adding a new enemy to the battle. After spending the night with Radovid, Jaskier loses Ciri, though he does realize that was what Radovid planned. Ciri has escaped, and, though killing Lydia briefly delays her, Yennefer ultimately finds Ciri. Rience reaches them as well, but Geralt arrives and beheads him. However, the family must separate as Yennefer returns to protect Aretuza while Geralt and Ciri try to escape. Yennefer joins the all-out battle between the Brotherhood and the Elves. In the chaos, Stregobor sacrifices himself, Vilgefortz recovers the Book of Monoliths, and Yennefer gets Tissaia out at the last minute. As they leave, Geralt and Ciri encounter Cahir, whom Ciri blames for destroying her home. However, Cahir, who has rethought his loyalties, surrenders to Ciri. But when the Elves find them, he temporarily rescinds the offer to protect her. Yet, the Elves are not Geralt and Ciri's only enemy. Vilgefortz finds them, and Geralt sends Ciri on alone. In the fight, Geralt is badly injured , and when Vilgefortz wins, he follows Ciri into the tunnels just before the tower explodes. In the end, the Elves leave without Ciri, the mages watch the destruction of Aretuza, and Triss finds an injured Geralt. Jaskier also discovers a distraught Radovid in the aftermath and gives him a way home despite their differences. Though everyone suspects Ciri is dead, she falls into the desert of Korath and must survive on her own. Throughout her journey, Ciri experiences various hallucinations, including long-dead family members, a unicorn, and a mysterious woman called Falka ( Hiftu Quasem ), a legendary figure who is considered a monster. Ciri's unicorn friend is attacked, and to heal it, she lets Falka tempt her into fire magic , scaring the unicorn. Though Falka tells her to give in to it, Ciri releases the magic quickly. The next thing Ciri remembers is waking up to strangers, who take her captive. 'The Witcher' Season 3's Finale Sets Up Big Threats for Every Character Henry Cavill as Geralt of Rivia fighting several knights in The Witcher Image via Netflix After the events at Aretuza, Tissaia dies by suicide over her immense guilt and Vilgefortz's betrayal. In the aftermath, Yennefer, Triss, and the other mages make it their mission to rebuild the Brotherhood and eliminate Vilgefortz. Meanwhile, Geralt heals from his wounds in Brokilon, where Jaskier brings the news that Nilfgaard has seemingly found Ciri. Yennefer visits him, with each blaming themselves for what happened to Ciri. She heals Geralt, and he promises to find Ciri while Yennefer builds a safe place for them to return to. In Redania, Vizimir accuses Dijkstra of failure, wanting Philippa killed as punishment. However, Philippa has Vizimir assassinated, making an unwilling Radovid the new king. Redania isn't the only country facing changes . Fringilla and Francesca, who reunited during the battle, propose a deal with Emhyr to make Fringilla the governor of Cintra, where the Elves can live. Emhyr gives them harsh terms, and still, Francesca is ready to agree until Fringilla reveals that Emhyr killed Francesca's baby , leading the mourning mother to swear revenge. Emhyr has a major win when Ciri seems to return home; however, the girl presented to him is Teryn , and Emhyr doesn't seem to realize it. The real Ciri is held captive until she teams up with another prisoner. The other prisoners' friends, a criminal group known as the Rats , come to save him, including Mistle ( Christelle Elwin ), whom Ciri briefly met before. In the fight, Ciri kills her captor, showing a more brutal side of herself and impressing the Rats. Now healed, Geralt leaves Brokilon to rescue who he thinks is Ciri from Emhyr's clutches . He and Jaskier pass a corrupt set of Nilfgaardian soldiers, and though Geralt manages to bribe them, the girl behind them cannot. Geralt takes action , forsaking his neutrality and killing the guards. His new ally, Milva ( Meng'er Zhang ), a skilled archer from Brokilon, also commits herself to Geralt's new cause. Between Geralt's determination to act, Yennefer's mission to rebuild, and Ciri's new companions, The Witcher Season 3 leaves many stories open, promising an action-packed return as the Netflix series moves towards its impending end . The Witcher Season 4 premieres October 30 on Netflix.
